assessment: The synthesis correctly preserves the concept-drift definition, monitoring limits, lack of universal thresholds, and lack of a direct controlled comparison. However, K0002/K0005 use a broad adaptive-soft-sensor taxonomy as though it were wholly distinct from base-model retraining, which conflicts with the frozen scope whenever those mechanisms change model parameters.

findings.target: 20_synthesis.K0002 / K0005: classification of moving-window, recursive-adaptation, and ensemble methods as lighter-weight alternatives to base-model retraining
evidence: 00_context.scope defines retraining as any use of new actual data that changes base prediction model parameters.
10_evidence.E0002 / SRC-0117 describes moving-window, recursive-adaptation, and ensemble approaches as broad soft-sensor adaptation categories.
20_synthesis.K0002 and K0005 use those broad categories to frame an alternative to base-model updating.
findings.impact: The synthesis can place methods that change the predictive model or its fitted parameters on the fixed-base-model side of the decision boundary. That blurs the frozen scope's three-way distinction and can distort the retraining gate in 30_analysis.

repair_direction.instruction: Rebuild the maintenance taxonomy around the frozen scope. Treat moving-window/recursive/ensemble methods only as background adaptation categories; any method that changes base-model parameters must be classified as model update/retraining under this Investigation. Keep only genuinely external post-prediction correction on the fixed-base comparator side, then rebuild 30_analysis.
